claim_boundary: Published Bitcoin calendar studies conflict: one 2013-2019 study reports no Halloween return anomaly and stronger calendar effects in conditional volatility, while a 2018-2024 multi-crypto study reports higher Halloween-period returns with higher risk and states that BTC is an exception to most-assets outperformance. This conflict permits one exact low-turnover replication, not a seasonal-alpha claim.

primary_sources.title: Calendar effects in Bitcoin returns and volatility
primary_sources.finding: The 2013-2019 analysis reports no evidence of a Bitcoin Halloween return anomaly and stronger calendar effects in conditional volatility.

primary_sources.title: Profitability and risk in cryptocurrency markets: testing the Halloween effect and investment strategies
primary_sources.finding: The 2018-2024 multi-crypto analysis reports higher Halloween-period returns with higher risk, but identifies BTC as an exception to most-assets Halloween outperformance.

primary_sources.title: Bitcoin time-of-day, day-of-week and month-of-year effects in returns and trading volume
primary_sources.finding: A seven-exchange high-frequency study reports time-specific return anomalies but no persistent return effects across time, while volume patterns were more persistent.

independence_and_duplicate_boundary.distinct_from_closed_turn_of_month: The closed turn-of-month family used a short last-day-plus-three-day window. This family uses one fixed six-month UTC season and cannot inherit or combine that result.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.distinct_from_closed_weekend_and_intrada: This family has no weekday or hour selection and cannot scan calendar subperiods.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.overlapping_published_outcomes: Both cited Bitcoin studies expose overlapping historical returns. Repository Design and Validation can only be replication/development evidence, never independent confirmation or OOS.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.prohibited_rescue: Do not move either boundary, select months, add January, quarter, weekday, trend, volatility, macro, on-chain or event interactions, invert the season, fractional-size or short after outcomes.

adversarial_prior: Continuous global BTC trading has no equity-market summer closure mechanism, so a traditional-market Halloween story may not transfer.
The strongest directly relevant older Bitcoin study reports no Halloween return anomaly.
The newer study used 2018-2024, overlapping the entire intended repository sample and therefore cannot validate it independently.
A six-month cash leg can reduce drawdown mechanically while forfeiting most bull-market upside; total PnL, Calmar and upside participation must pass together.
With only four Design and two Validation seasonal episodes, annual breadth and episode concentration are severe limits even if aggregate PnL improves.
stop_conditions: Before reading repository BTC outcomes, freeze exactly one hypothesis, one manifest, one runner hash and all Design, Validation, cost, path-risk, breadth, concentration and determinism gates.
Use exactly November through April long and May through October zero-yield cash at UTC month boundaries; no alternative dates, months, direction or sizing.
Stop NO_CANDIDATE on any Design or Validation matched-capital total-PnL, drawdown, Calmar, upside, annual-breadth, concentration or determinism failure.
Do not open post-2024 outcomes. Any historical pass remains REPORTED_NOT_ACTIVATED and needs untouched independent OOS.
